THE THREE FILES OF THIS FOLDER — the strong model of the photo window's „Entfernen"
====================================================================================

moebius_encoder.onnx   68,498,193 bytes
moebius_decoder.onnx   99,187,044 bytes
moebius_unet.onnx     455,522,843 bytes

    THEY ARE NOT IN THE REPOSITORY. The largest is more than a file may
    weigh on its way through GitHub (100 MB), so the three are laid into
    this folder on the server BY HAND, once (.gitignore names them). The
    server offers the model only when all three are there
    (includes/helpers.php, inpaint_strong_offered); the browser holds them
    to exactly the sizes above (assets/js/inpaint.js, STRONG_FILES), so a
    file cut short on its way up is noticed by the download.

    Moebius, "0.2B Lightweight Image Inpainting Framework with 10B-Level
    Performance", Duan, Xu, Liu, Ruan, Chen, Wang — Huazhong University of
    Science and Technology and VIVO AI Lab, ECCV 2026,
    https://github.com/hustvl/Moebius, arXiv 2606.19195. Code AND weights
    under the Apache License 2.0; commercial use of the weights and of the
    pictures they make is allowed (the repository's own words).

    Converted from PyTorch to ONNX (opset 18, static 512 x 512, fp32) by
    Simon Willison, https://huggingface.co/simonw/Moebius-ONNX, Apache
    License 2.0: vae_encoder.onnx, vae_decoder.onnx, unet.onnx — the
    denoiser re-exported there without its Conv3d steps, which Safari's
    WebGPU could not compile. Which of the upstream checkpoints was
    converted is not stated there.

    THESE COPIES WERE MADE HERE from those three: every float32 weight of
    4096 values and more stored as half floats, with a Cast back to float32
    in front of whatever reads it (pack.py below, rule "fp16"). onnxruntime
    folds the cast once, at load, so the arithmetic is the original's; only
    the stored numbers are rounded. 1.27 GB became 623 MB.

    MEASURED on 14.11.2026, twelve large and very large holes in two of
    Christian's pictures, each variant against the fp32 files with the same
    random start (Chromium, WebGPU). The fill's mean colour, in tone values
    of 255, on average / at the worst:
        fp16 throughout (these files)             623 MB   0.05 / 0.14
        denoiser's ff convs int8, rest fp16       547 MB   0.59 / 1.09
        denoiser int8, VAE fp16                   412 MB   1.09 / 2.50
        denoiser's convs int8, rest fp16          439 MB   1.12 / 2.33
        int8 throughout                           334 MB   1.71 / 6.02
        for scale: fp32 with ANOTHER random start          16   / 43
    Unlike LaMa (assets/vendor/lama) there is no small sensitive group to
    spare: smaller is a little less exact, whichever layers are taken.
    Christian chose the 623 MB: the same picture as the full model.
    Firefox 159 computes the same fill as Chromium, to the last tone value.

    The sampling loop is no part of these files: assets/js/moebius.js, with
    the numbers it must keep and why fewer steps were not taken.

The runtime they run on is the one in assets/vendor/lama (onnxruntime-web,
MIT License; see LICENSE.txt there).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------
pack.py — how the three files were made
(Python 3.12, onnx, numpy; python pack.py unet.onnx moebius_unet.onnx fp16,
 and the same for vae_encoder.onnx and vae_decoder.onnx)

"""Store a model's large float weights smaller — any graph, any consumer.

Every float32 initializer of at least MIN_VALUES values is replaced by a
small chain that yields the same tensor UNDER THE SAME NAME, so nothing that
reads it has to change:
    fp16   the values as half floats            -> Cast(to float)
    int8   blockwise integers, one scale per 64 -> DequantizeLinear -> Reshape
           values along the flattened rest          (needs opset 21)
onnxruntime folds either chain back to plain float32 once, at load (for int8
the session must set session.disable_quant_qdq = 1), so the arithmetic is
the original's; only the stored numbers are rounded.

A rule is a list "pattern=how,pattern=how,...,how": the first pattern (a
regular expression on "<tensor name> @<ops that read it>") that matches
decides, the bare last entry is for everything else. how: fp16 | int8 | keep.

usage: python pack.py <in.onnx> <out.onnx> <rule>
"""
import re
import sys

import numpy as np
import onnx
from onnx import TensorProto, helper, numpy_helper

MIN_VALUES = 4096
BLOCK = 64


def main(src, dst, rule):
    parts = rule.split(",")
    rules = [(re.compile(p.rsplit("=", 1)[0]), p.rsplit("=", 1)[1]) for p in parts[:-1]]
    default = parts[-1]
    model = onnx.load(src)
    g = model.graph
    kept, added_inits, added_nodes = [], [], []
    tally = {}
    # Who reads a tensor: a pattern may ask for it, as "name @Conv,Gemm".
    readers = {}
    for n in g.node:
        for i in n.input: readers.setdefault(i, set()).add(n.op_type)
    for t in g.initializer:
        if t.data_type != TensorProto.FLOAT or int(np.prod(t.dims)) < MIN_VALUES:
            kept.append(t); continue
        key = t.name + " @" + ",".join(sorted(readers.get(t.name, ())))
        how = next((h for rx, h in rules if rx.search(key)), default)
        w = numpy_helper.to_array(t)
        tally.setdefault(how, [0, 0, 0]); tally[how][0] += 1; tally[how][1] += w.nbytes
        if how == "keep":
            kept.append(t); tally[how][2] += w.nbytes; continue
        if how == "fp16":
            h = numpy_helper.from_array(w.astype(np.float16), t.name + "__h")
            added_inits.append(h)
            added_nodes.append(helper.make_node("Cast", [h.name], [t.name], to=TensorProto.FLOAT, name=t.name + "__cast"))
            tally[how][2] += w.size * 2
            continue
        assert how == "int8", how
        rows = w.shape[0] if w.ndim > 1 else 1
        k = w.size // rows
        nblocks = -(-k // BLOCK)
        padded = np.zeros((rows, nblocks * BLOCK), np.float32); padded[:, :k] = w.reshape(rows, k)
        blocks = padded.reshape(rows, nblocks, BLOCK)
        scale = np.abs(blocks).max(axis=2) / 127
        scale[scale == 0] = 1.0
        q = np.clip(np.round(blocks / scale[..., None]), -128, 127).astype(np.int8).reshape(rows, nblocks * BLOCK)[:, :k]
        added_inits += [numpy_helper.from_array(q, t.name + "__q"), numpy_helper.from_array(scale.astype(np.float32), t.name + "__s"),
                        numpy_helper.from_array(np.array(w.shape, np.int64), t.name + "__shape")]
        added_nodes += [helper.make_node("DequantizeLinear", [t.name + "__q", t.name + "__s"], [t.name + "__dq"], axis=1, block_size=BLOCK, name=t.name + "__dqn"),
                        helper.make_node("Reshape", [t.name + "__dq", t.name + "__shape"], [t.name], name=t.name + "__rs")]
        tally[how][2] += q.size + scale.size * 4
    del g.initializer[:]; g.initializer.extend(kept + added_inits)
    nodes = list(g.node); del g.node[:]; g.node.extend(added_nodes + nodes)
    if "int8" in tally:
        for o in model.opset_import:
            if o.domain in ("", "ai.onnx"): o.version = max(o.version, 21)
    onnx.save(model, dst)
    for how, (count, before, after) in tally.items():
        print(f"  {how}: {count} tensors, {before / 1e6:.1f} MB -> {after / 1e6:.1f} MB")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(*sys.argv[1:4])
